name: Atlassian Design System
tagline: A productivity-suite system that takes content and editing seriously.
origin: Atlassian's design system grew alongside Jira, Confluence, Trello, and Bitbucket. It exists to make those products feel like one product family despite different histories and architectures.
governance: Centralized design system team with strong product-team partnership. Public design tokens; component libraries shipped as `@atlaskit/*` packages.
knownFor: Editor and content components — Atlassian's rich-text editor patterns are publicly documented in unusual detail.
Fast token system that supports their light + dark + high-contrast themes cleanly.
Strong empty-state and zero-data patterns — critical for productivity tools.
underrated: Avatar groups, mention chips, and presence indicators — small components that productivity apps need but rarely document well.
The publicly readable rationale behind their token names is good study material.
watchOutsFor: Several `@atlaskit/*` packages are in different stages of maturity; check the per-component status.
The system is built around productivity-tool workflows; lifting it into a marketing surface requires re-thought visual rhythm.
evaluationGuidance: Pick this if you're building productivity, collaboration, or knowledge tools. The editor and content patterns alone make it worth studying for any team building text-heavy product surfaces.

components.name: Editor
components.note: Modular rich-text editor with mentions, commands, and collaborative editing primitives.

components.name: Side Navigation
components.note: Multi-level nav patterns built for products with deep IA.
